While there may be certain bits of knowledge on the team, I believe in the era of the internet and with intelligent effective people who have learned how to learn, there are better categorizations of work functions outside of basic knowledge. Certain people seem to be better inclined to some of these than others depending on desire, personality type, time of day, etc. They are as follows:

1. Identify + enable. This is grossly lumped into a category known as marketing. And marketing as a category of work is an absolute travesty. The current paradigm is that we spend oodles of money to get the attention of people to “build an audience” in which we slice and dice categorizations to make hypotheses about human behavior. There is a better way. The best community builders implicitly understand that to form a new community, one has to combine an overlap of two or more existing communities. You convince active members in different communities that they may get some benefit from interacting with each other in a third space and set up a context in which it is easy to interact in that place. That third space is the environment where you’re building something. This skillset is best measured by the number of active people in the overlap of communities and how that number changes over time through enabling activities.

2. Search + select. This is a sales or research function. The people who are best at this are ones who easily create lists of options, then narrow down the scope of that list to find a desired result. Salespeople do this by going from a large number of prospects down to a select few. The most important skill here is listening. These people are measured in the first order by activity, the second order by the rate, and the third order by their discernment in listening which leads to results.

3. Prototype + test. These type of folks feel wrong if they haven’t made something by the end of the day. They’re constantly creating something new and putting it out into the world. It could be writing or designs or physical prototypes, the only thing they’re measured on is how often and how much.

4. Measure + optimize. This is the anthropologist, the editor, the keeper of the time, the operational guru who tracks everything, makes sure everything has a proper place and constitently takes the pulse of the team to identify places where there could be improvement. This sometimes takes the form of documentarian, problem identification and sets the right metrics to measure. They keep incrementally improving on the task in front of them.

5. Organize + teach. The coach, the manager, the champion. This person picks the right people then is in charge of ensuring the team stays on task and is focused on the right things. They help unblock problems and find ways to improve the communication, coordination or composition of the team. They can add or remove team members, mediate conflict and delve into strategies to improve the meta process of the thing being built.

For my methods of making I like getting feedback 1–1, working in teams of 3 on one of the specialties to break disagreements, and organizing in groups of ~10 (with the understanding that at least ~50% tend to not show up) to make sure there’s at least the basic specialties covered for bigger long-term projects. The people matter so much + part of why I was a participant in the analog astronaut community was to investigate how we might construct high-performing teams in stressful environments. Picking the right people has been mattering more and more to me over time.

item.title: Toothpox
item.content:encoded:
Her pillow was a bit rocky, so much so she couldn’t sleep. Tossing and turning Claire grew frustrated and jumped out of bed and began pacing her room, muttering to herself.

If her calculations were correct, tomorrow would be a giant payday, she just had to convince her overeager mind to calm down.

She licked her lips, rubbing her hands together like she’d seen in old films like some sort of greed-driven megalomaniac. She coughed slightly and another tooth fell out.

The toothpox had run through her school, and she knew that the tooth fairy was going to pay up. Due to inflation, a tooth had a going rate of $5/tooth, and with the scheme she cooked up with her friends, they were yanking teeth out left and right from friends like regular dentists.

She collected 107 before she realized she had to find some quiet way of transporting these mouth stones.

The virus had run amok among her 3rd grade class and just like sharks, the kids needed to lose their teeth or else suffer the consequences. Orthodontists didn’t know what to do with them. Headgear was nonexistant and everyone had a lisp.

She carried the 107 teeth home in her backpack, pockets and wherever she could stash these mouth jewels. Her mom wondered why she immediately sped upstairs to hide her treasure.

Tonight was the time that the tooth fairy would return with money aplenty. About $535 if her multiplication was correct (and she had checked and double-checked her math). If that dumb fairy didn’t pay up, she’d have hell to pay. Her friends were all expecting their cut. She bet all of her own teeth on the money she was going to receive.

She took a few deep breaths. Let’s think of a plan B. If that dumb fairy never shows, then she’ll have to do something with all these canines. She’d have to make necklaces or charms or potentially turn them into bracelets or maybe even bedazzle notebooks with some superglue.

Finally tired from the anxiety and stress of the big score, Claire settled down into a restless sleep, dreaming of all her teeth falling out.

She awoke with a start, quickly checking under her pillow. The big pillowcase filled with tonsils was gone and in its place was a note that merely read: IOU.

Turns out that she was going to have to grow some more teeth at school today.

item.title: Dimensions
item.content:encoded:
Give yourself a task to write about the description of making a box. Not just any box. The most beautiful box in all existence. And make the person making the box someone who was heartbroken once. Someone who loved in all their stolen glory. Someone who was raised religious and lost it and found it again in the box making. Someone who wished for the life of them that they could compress all the meaning and chaos and beauty in this world down into a particular shape so long as that shape was a box.

Maybe it’s a curse. This kind of box brain. Maybe they’re among a bunch of people who don’t see right-angles, who really enjoy curves. Their box-making is lost on the world of curvaceous folks (in the figurative sense) because there’s really nowhere a box could fit.

As the author, it’s my job to torture this person. To place them at a fair for people that make objects. To have a crowd come on by to admire the spheres next to them. To have them sit and hope and sit and hope until the sun goes down to only have one person come by with their wife and say “i have no clue how it would fit by the fireplace”

Have them pack up their boxes, none of them quite as beautiful as they expected and travel home to an empty bubble. The walls shrinking in as they weep and imagine the life that they hoped for. The dream of making the perfect cube a box to put everything they could ever want inside.

And at the lowest point there needs to be some kind of turn. Something to make it so that the box-maker isn’t completely destroyed by the steamroller of the world otherwise that’d just be cruel. To heap on so much pain and to never have a glimmer of a way out would be to imagine a world that is too real and too monstrous for one to comprehend (plus nobody would want to read about that reality). We read to escape the things that chase us, to dodge and run like hell for the horizon where there’s a chance of it being different, never again to be devoured.

The box-maker wanted things to be different. Realize that as the author even your imagination sometimes doesn’t know ways to make things different. Suffer the same kind of sadness as your character as you watch him take out his sandpaper and start sanding the edges of his beautiful boxes down until he’s in a pile of dust and everything is a sphere.

Maybe he sells some of the sanded down boxes at a discount. Maybe he becomes an accountant like his mother always said he should be. Maybe he puts them in his little round garage and comes back to them years later after his mother dies. He unpacks these sad sanded spheres and thinks to himself that he would try again.

Here’s the spice: bring back the hope from the outside like a wrecking ball to break the norm. The perfect oval picture frame of sameness just doesn’t seem right, what you need is violence. Everything is but a destructive act away from change.

da Vinci once spent an entire lifetime trying to square a circle. He drew endless pictures of the combination of two shapes, measuring out the frame of a man stuck between two positions then circling the whole thing as if to say “here it is! all of life right here! pay attention please!” and then he died.

All the years of toil and effort came back in that moment. He begins with framing right angles, making the perfect boxes for each one of the broken spheres. Gently he places his old dreams inside each box, a perfectly made home for every single one.

Finally, he frames up a much larger box. One to put himself inside. He steps in and closes his eyes.

Now is where you bring it home. The whole shebang. The ending to make it all worth it. The reason why the people came here in the first place. You’re making a box and it needs to fit in the fireplace of the mind. It needs to make sense in the context of the world or else the absurdity of it all will kill you. It might kill your characters and you have to go on living with the understanding that you’re a murderer, that there’s blood on the page, that every time you try to make the most beautiful box it just turns into a sphere. You’re the Vitruvian man and you don’t quite fit the perfect shape.

So the man gets in the box but the box could be anything. It could be the very best toilet in the world and he solves sanitation for millions. It could be a coffin and he dies. It could be a platform on which he finally is able to shout to all the people who walked by his stand at the market “look at how amazing everything could be if you just looked!”

But today the box is just a box and he steps out of it, a bit disappointed at himself for trying again. He lifts up the box and throws it in frustration on top of the rest of them.

Astoundingly, it doesn’t slide down. It doesn’t fall. It remains on top of one of the other boxes. The man can’t believe his eyes. Never before had he seen something like what he is witnessing.

At this point we’re seeing the magic. At this point the realization, the recognition and reckoning that everything has changed after this moment. You see our little box maker, living in a spherical world, had just discovered dimensionality.

The box maker began stacking the boxes, one on top of the other, and began to climb, reaching higher than anyone had ever gone before. Laughing in the sun.

item.title: I Lived on an All Algae Diet for A Week and Didn’t Die
item.description: I Lived on an All Algae Diet for A Week and Didn’t Die
item.content:encoded:
It’s been a month and I’ve been quietly testing out various aspects of going on an all algae diet as a means of generating data for an IRB (Institutional Review Board) as well as prototyping recipes using nothing but algae and water.

I think scientific research doesn’t often prototype and I really wanted to take an easier and more iterative approach. Since this is an N=1 study, I don’t have many challenges to overcome in regards to approvals except to showcase the potential downsides of the diet. That means that I get to mess with myself as a guinea pig. I decided to do a week of eating nothing but slime to see how my body responded and as a means of gearing up to longer tests and better recipes. Fun fun fun.

I kicked off the week with a 2-day fast to stabilize my gut microbiome + get a metabolic panel prior to changing my diet over. I’m an omnivore, leaning vegetarian. I guess I would categorize myself as “freegan” where I live in a vegan household and only eat meat if I’m out with other people + there aren’t other options. I tend to eat anything that’s going to be thrown away and when traveling I never make a fuss about food. I don’t have any allergies, and I’m quite regular so my gut microbiome is seemingly healthy. I eat eggs on toast for breakfast normally, with some kind of quick smoothie, salad or sandwich for lunch and a heavier dinner with a main protein, roast vegetables and grains.

As a means of starting from this baseline, I kicked off the week drinking nothing but water (with some electrolytes). I took a preliminary gut microbiome sample, started my continuous glucose measurement with Levels, and some initial metabolic testing via Forward:

Blood albumin levels were a bit out of whack here because of slight dehydration. Besides that, everything looked average and stable.

I was a bit concerned about my liver enzymes changing over the week which had happened before when I tested some AFA previously (I do NOT recommend to eat AFA or anything wild harvested from Klamanth Lake) so I wanted to make note of my AST and ALT. Kidney function (eGFRcr) was normal.

I ran into some trouble with my doctor at Forward on scheduling an end metabolic test within the time window of the diet. I think I’ll shift over to getting a paid metabolic screen from Quest or Labcorp in the future to account for the timing of the diet. In addition, I’ll attempt to get more metabolites tested like my thyroid levels to check up on any excess iodine in my system. I’m also quite interested in what other tests I should run during the next iteration of the diet; please let me know if you have any thoughts on testing!

I started the fast on a Friday night and carried it through over the weekend. Initially I was in good spirits, spending time with friends, especially since I ate a high-protein meal as my last meal prior to the diet. As you can see, my weight dropped dramatically from 172 to 167 lbs over the course of 2 days. I was drinking 3+ liters of water daily so I’m guessing that this is when my body was kicking over into ketosis. I was starting to burn some of my fat reserves. With a quick check of my ketone measurement device, that seemed to be true:

Optimal ketosis during fasting diets is defined as between 0.5mmol/L — 3mmol/L which means I was a bit out of that range during the start of the diet.

I’m not entirely a fan of this method of measuring ketones as I have to jab myself and bleed a drop on the detector. The breath measurement tool seemed easier and would allow me to take more data points.

When I couple this kind of measurement with my continuous glucose sensor, it forms a more detailed picture of my blood glucose/ketone amounts and how that corresponds to overall energy changes and weight change. I’d like to test my blood glucose measurements using a finger prick as well as my Levels/Dexcom continuous blood glucose monitor just to see how the balance shifts over time.

I expected to be in ketosis for the majority of the diet as the carbohydrate component of the algae is quite minimal if I’m not consuming large amounts of seaweed. It seemed like my average glucose was around 90 mg/dL which wasn’t ideal. This led to a lot of brain fog and a lack of concentration, something that might be helped in the future with more carbohydrate inputs from seaweed snacks. There were very few glucose spikes during the diet as I never consumed large quantities of food, merely snacking on small things throughout the day.

The fast went relatively quickly, I went through all my normal exercise routines, averaging at least 10,000 steps daily with energy waning a bit on Sunday. I tend to weight lift three times per week, alternate with cardio (stationary bike mostly) and have a rest day mixed in there. I definitely didn’t keep to this as the week went on and my energy waned. Luckily, San Francisco is an incredibly walkable city so I got a chance to get my steps in. I’m wondering if I should be testing my muscle mass output and trying to find a good standardized way to do that via exercise. I think one of the best methods might be getting a distal strength (grip) measurement device or following in the path of Bryan Johnson and using the ACSM guidelines. This is definitely something I’ll add to my measurements for the next algae diet testing session.

My sleep patterns were all over the place which also heavily affected the start of the diet. Sleep is really the foundation of health so I made a note to standardize sleep in the future, controlling to minimize the variability in when I go to bed, wake up and the length of time spent asleep. I tend to use a facemask and earplugs but sleep in a room that borders a busy street. Another factor at play is that I just moved to a new city, and was sleeping in a somewhat unfamiliar environment. I wasn’t getting good sleep which is something I’ll make sure to take into account for future experiments, trying to control for standardizing my sleep patterns. One of the algae supplements I could take to better improve my overall sleep patterns would be Ecklonia cava, a seaweed which has certain compounds that mimic Ambien and could help me get to sleep faster.

Before starting, I had charted out the basic nutrients I needed for the diet but I was lacking in calories in particular which were supposed to come from algae oil. I couldn’t find a good source of algae oil so I opted to use cultured oil instead (virtually the same) from Zero Acre Farms. Each day I was supposed to consume 2000 calories (albeit a bit low for my activity levels) which corresponds to at least 1000 cals or 125 ml of oil daily.

(ignore the percentages here + I may need to adjust for exercise + improve my overall spreadsheets based on what ingredients/recipes I have on-hand)

I’m fascinated by N=1 studies like this one and would love to attempt to replicate something similar with algae-based foods. One of the harder parts of the diet was trying to come up with recipes that would meet all of my nutritional requirements in a way that wasn’t just eating powders and chugging water. I had all the components of a complete diet but needed to find a way to make things palatable. The recipe development took 2–3 hours at minimum each time I entered the kitchen which was really untenable with my work schedule. This is why my actual caloric consumption hovered around ~1000 calories each day, definitely well under what I wanted or needed.

The number one question I got during the diet was about my number twos:

I got a really great poop tracking app that measures my bowel movements. Over the course of the week I only had two — the first seemed like a residual from the prior week but the second was interesting. A lot more green in color but besides that completely normal ranking a 5 on the Bristol Stool scale. I sent my microbiome out for analysis and discovered that my gut bacteria changed significantly just over a few days. Pathobionts went down significantly and gut diversity went up, indicating an overall beneficial change. That could be do to depressing my gut microbiome with the fast, however I was excited to see a slight change in the bacterial makeup of the gut with new species colonizing my colon (;D). I’m assuming that the effect would be even greater over time.

My starting heart rate variability was normal (although I’d like my resting/sleeping heart rate to be a lot lower. That just means I need a bit more exercise).

My ending heart rate variability was elevated which might indicate a stressed state. The change in diet, the lack of sleep, the consistent exercise, the challenges with getting enough calories… in the future I’d want to see a stable hrv when conducting the diet.

I attempted to keep a food journal and conduct urinalysis during the diet but had difficulty keeping track. I was using a notes app on my phone but if you have any specific recommendations let me know. I think in the future this is something I’ll be way more diligent about as urinalysis can yield some interesting insights about mineral content in the pee and bloodstream.

I took standard blood pressure, temperature and pulse oximetry data every morning. Not much change here on a day-to-day but still good measurement tools to check for general baseline health.

I played around a bit with my roommates AI recipe generator to see if I could come up with a number of algae-only recipes. As for recipes, these are two that I’m particularly fond of: algae bacon pancakes and kombu broth. The first was a major challenge in getting the dough to rise properly. I think I might try with baking powder in the future which might be okay under standard diet rules as I could be flexible in terms of basic kitchen chemicals. Test of algae pancakes:

  • 2 tsp algae oil
  • 1/4 cup chlorella
  • 1/2 tsp iota carrageenan
  • 1/2 cup water
  • 1 tsp blue spirulina
  • 1 tsp agar agar

Add oil to the pan Heat up + flip Fry dulse bacon to serve on the side Enjoy!

The second recipe has become a staple. Similar to bone broth, this kombu stock is incredibly filling, super nutritionally dense and easy to make.

You start by boiling water, then adding a few blades of dried kombu, wakame, arame, and dulse to the pot then reducing to a simmer and cooking for 30 minutes minimum. Strain out the algae leave + enjoy! I started drinking this soup stock daily and it was incredibly filling. I would love to do a proper analysis to see what kind of nutritional value it has in there.

In conclusion the prototype week of eating only algae helped me learn a ton that will inform future experiments. In particular I’m quite excited to play around with new recipes with a group of people, embrace new measurement techniques and attempt another prototype week of the diet in October.

I gave a brief talk about the diet and what I learned here. Super excited to share more results and experiments in the future. If you’re interested in getting involved, follow this link to participate:

https://forms.gle/k9dPjnC4z7ZkLuaT9

item.title: Dave Grohl was standing in the doorway of the stable
item.description: Dave Grohl was standing in the doorway of the stable
item.content:encoded:
Dave Grohl was standing in the doorway of the stable, staring at me while I had my hand halfway inside a horse.

“Umm… hi. You’re Dave Grohl.”

“I’ve been told.”

“I’m gonna grab something from the truck.”

My mind raced frantically. This was a rock god, there goes my hero, Dave-fucking-Grohl, the man, the myth, the legend, all bearded tattooed glory of him and there I was covered in horse fluids trembling like the 16-year-old punk kid that I was.

I used to make trips out to LA on break to visit my uncles. It was a good trip, something where I could hang out in the sunshine during breaks from school and since I was interested in medicine, I would go on veterinary rounds with my uncle Neil. He was a horse vet for the rich and tanned, and drove his 2004 Durango up and down the valley pushing steroids and ketamine for everyone from Schwarzenegger to Regis. Horses that is.

Since he worked 6 days a week I’d get up at the asscrack of dawn and hang with him in the back, kicking it in the jump seat of the car. Hugo his assistant would be driving while Neil fielded calls. We’d talk about life in between hopping from barn to barn, discussing family lore, his practice, questions about what it means to really work on something you love, living in Los Angeles, and shooting the shit about things that a 16-year-old would like, namely dirt on my parents and music.

At the time I was playing in an alternative rock/punk band in high school called Sane Asylum. We’d been jamming most every night for months and started playing some shows in the area. I was the singer-songwriter writing teenage angst songs while hiding cases of beer that we stole from my parents in the bass drum. Music was a big part of my life and I had these giant headphones where I’d rock out to some of the classics like AC/DC, Green Day, Nirvana and the Foo Fighters.

And here I was, quivering standing next to my uncle helping grab gear from the truck. Dave Grohl grew up in the same hometown as me, snuck into the same venues like the 9:30 Club using a fake ID same as me, went crazy in the same suburban wasteland as me, and I had the good fortune to bump into him at some stupid barn in Malibu while watching his daughter’s horseback riding practice?

Fuck me. Make a move, Roth.

I asked my uncle, “What kind of celebrities do you normally bump into during your veterinary rounds?”

He shrugged and rattled off a list of clients that included Flea from the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Steven Tyler from Aerosmith, and the founder of the Cheesecake Factory.

Rock royalty and the Cheesecake Factory. Maybe being a vet was the life for me. I imagined hanging in a hot tub with these gods while eating white chocolate raspberry cheesecake and being serenaded with anthems of the 90s.

“Can you grab these needles for me?” Neil tossed a handful of syringes my way along with some gauze. Loaded up, I stumbled back over to the barn.

What was I going to say? I needed to figure out how to calm down.

All of the sudden it struck me, the immortal words of a classic children’s novel that I had been saying to myself while scooping horse shit earlier:

Everybody poops.

It was going to be okay, just remember that Dave Grohl, founder of the supergroup Them Crooked Vultures, is a person too and he definitely has squeezed out a stinky one before.

Dave was watching his daughter trot around the ring in circles looking hella bored when I sidled up.

“So… I just got in from Annandale, Virginia. Visiting my uncle.”

“Cool… *awkward silence* …umm are those needles you’re carrying?”

“I’m gonna go.”

As I walked away, I realized that there was no need to be scared of Dave Grohl, former drummer of Nirvana. Probably just that morning he had laid out a stinky lincoln log in the commode.

After that, I’ve never been afraid of meeting anyone again.

item.title: It comes in stages
item.content:encoded:
First there’s the denial. The idea that you’re ending is incomprehensible. You had wondered what forever felt like and this was as close to the taste of it as you had ever experienced.

The anger at betrayal is felt deep to the core. The shock and revulsion will fester if it doesn’t boil. You ask why and there is no answer.

Finally some truth. You learn that these things are inevitable. That the idea you had of someone is but a flashlight in a dark room. You only saw one part of them, never the whole picture. Now with the full picture, you see how they’re broken and offer to pick up the pieces. Bargaining the future for the past, trying to piece together the bits that were kind and happy and true.

I’m in the sadness now. All-encompassing like a shroud it weighs heavy on my shoulders like a cold blanket. This new city is like shedding skin. This new person is cocooned, goo-like and transforming before my very eyes.

Time brings it back around. Our minds were not meant to remember forever. We are made for change. Hearts change. Cities change. People change. They end again and again and again. Back to the beginning.

When I was 20, my former lover’s lover killed himself.
We drink milkshakes every time we talk.
We hardly ever talk about him.
That kind of conversation deserves something stronger.
Whiskey.

When I was 20, my friend’s friend skull cracked.
She fell down a set of stairs and dashed her head
against the corner in front of me.
Art school.
Dark red wine.

When I was 20, my sister’s role model’s heart burst.
All he wanted to do was to heal children.
He didn’t drink.
But he laughed.
Shirley Temple.

When I was 20, my father’s mother was eaten.
Cancer comes slow and steady.
She stole a stein for me from her homeland.
She told me with a wink that no matter what I do, don’t get caught.
Radler.

When I was 20, my cousin’s husband was lost.
His life was art.
He was a humble fighter.
You can see love in his work.
Craft Beer.

When I was 20, the old me died like a garage sale.
With each person that left a little bit of the old disappeared.
An empty room.
An empty barrel.
Moonshine.

So raise a glass.
Toast the unknown and throw it down your throat
and let it echo in your chest.
Drink in your people until you drown and learn how to breathe them.
Drunk and unsteady you find new liquor.
Let it happen.
It’ll be okay.

Life is better with a buzz anyway

She shatters like toy planes
drops like stones
color drains
like melting crayons

Broken glass melodies play
on barefoot dreams
swallow my shadows
taste rusted machines

Drown in gravel
grey swollen riptide
pulls you under
bones for eyes

flay faces
peel me tangerine
rip floorboard smiles
handful of sertraline

we
echo genetic sparks
white-hot thunder pieces
combust fallen apart

item.title: Achylotropic
item.content:encoded:
I want to drive until I see snow
tie my blankets together and climb out the window
catapult into a careening car
headlights blinking just like stars

The branches are daggers cut my teeth on the cold
body so old
mind like a tumor always ready to grow
Radio
broken and stuck
playing Christmas music on repeat
my dumb luck
underneath frozen rivers fish sleep swimming letting the current carry

I get out and forget to lock it
sink my Popsicle toes into the sand
hands in my pockets

I’m Vitamin D deficient
but want to swallow the sun
I hope that the reflection off the moon is sufficient
horizon makes sky and water one
I feel omniscient
winter heart beats like a drum

the entire ocean is frozen
I start to run
on ice
skittering
sliding glass past bare feet
slice
splinter crack fracture
gravity in flight
mirror has broken
water a hand
gripping vice
filling tight
sound mouth suffer smother mother moth candle black night

the sun won’t ever come back
and that’s alright

item.title: Boxing Day
item.content:encoded:
The days after Christmas are some of the saddest of the year.
The streets lined with discarded Christmas trees, relatives departed,
and you’re left with shredded wrapping paper and leftovers to eat.

It’s in those days that I think the entire world is holding its breath.
It’s as if the week between Christmas and New Year’s is forgotten time,
time on the brink of the precipice of a new age,
time lost and shoved under the rug because
the New Time will be so much better, so much cleaner, so much nicer.

I feel so bad for that forlorn felled forest lying on curbsides around the world.
I wish I could gather up the boughs of holly, the unkissed mistletoe, the poinsettias that were purchased from that marching band sale.
I wish I could gather them all up and have a trillion-watt generator and power all the tangled mess of wires and bulbs, all the spotlit nativity scenes.
I wish I could place them all so it seems like they’re having a party in the middle of this forest, that the
angels are doing the limbo with the three wise men.
Jacob and Mary have snuck off under the mistletoe.
Jesus is in the arms of an inflatable snowman.
Everyone has too much old eggnog and fruitcake.
Everyone wraps themselves up to pretend to be gifts to the world.

I want to make the world’s largest bonfire out of all the discarded Christmas trees.
It’d smell like a cleaning commercial.
We’d have people come for miles around to make s’mores.
It’d be so warm that we could stay outside all winter and not have to worry about shoveling snow.
We could dance around the fire in our new clothes and PJs and only our socks if we wanted to.

How come we always have to get socks as gifts?

The week spent in limbo, in celebration, in mourning for a spent Christmas ends with December.
You expect something different but nothing ever changes.
The Christmas trees are picked up by the garbage men and the lights are taken down.
The relatives pack up and friends go away.
It gets quiet again.
The trees grow.

We can only take so much celebration.

item.title: Carrion
item.content:encoded:
My mouth is dry
My hands are numb
Body dumb head hung
Let the air out of my tires
Deflate mate
You can’t keep running to and
From places until you drop
Dead weight at your feet
Pick me up like a carcass
Nothing but meat
Spit and spin until I’m cooked
Carry on

item.title: Chick Flick
item.content:encoded:
As I lay here
in your dark theater
bum knees to chest
as previews of fantasies play
across these sheets
patient
when you’ll be done
editing yourself back together
in the bathroom

like the tiled mosaic
of the sweating linoleum
you’re smooth white feverish
waiting for me to slip and fall

Too late.
I’ve banged my knee
so I’m one short
which only makes me need you more

You are a quilt made of pictures that are stitched together
with hopes and dreams so tightly bound that they blend
into the world’s best romantic comedy.

I want to wrap myself up in you.

You open the door of the bathroom and lay your glasses next to mine.
Frame by frame.
Reel me in with your scent
condense my focus down to 80mm
and I can feel your box office hit
my lips ushers for your hips
So shhhh as my hands slip
she just wants a taste

scars from past lovers can never be erased

item.title: Christmas Day Meal
item.content:encoded:
Slicing beats
sweet hands
slightly sugared white snow
fingers peeling pomegranates
ice cold water split open
cut palm don’t notice
red
down garbage disposal
bleeding
stains on hands and clothes
from the meal
cherry tomatoes pop and gush
juice dribbles down chin
blood orange pulp
purple carrots crunch
dark corn shine
sagging roasted red peppers
bitter bone-white radishes
ruby on the inside
wilted spinach and guacamole
a true Christmas
macabre meal
single rose centerpiece
knife flashes
massacred plates
lips dried and cracked
bag it up
wash stains off hands
clean remnants away
down garbage disposal

for dessert:
red velvet cake marbled
like raw meat
cherry icing
bowls stained off-pink

item.title: Ember
item.content:encoded:
I watched stars being born today.

We were staring up
after the fire had crumbled to embers.
Just you, me
and the stars

There’s a cluster of nebulae out past Sagittarius
that are a nursery
to beacons of light
in the vast cold of space

Did you know
that voyager has that picture
of a Buddhist monk setting himself on fire?
The graphic scene immortalized
for all eternity on the laser-etched disk of memory
sent hurtling at a million miles an hour

It’s a lifeboat of humanity,
an idea to leave a mark
a small coal
black on black

Chances are that it’ll end up at that nebula one day
and dance with a star
its fingers pulling the hope of mankind
down with cold, serious gravity
burning up a painting of
Joan of Arc at the stake
that Buddhist monk
a child covered in Agent Orange
napalm
the books at Krystallnacht
a cross
on the lawn
when our lips touched
kerosene
spark
phoenix phoenix phoenix
memory
to a supernova flame

We lace fingers around a coal
it burns infinity into our souls

And the stars watch hungry

item.title: Flies
item.content:encoded:
My girlfriend told me yesterday about a girl
who split her lip
reciting the alphabet backwards
and got her mouth sewn up
and got all drugged up
and slept for days
but when she awoke
her lips were infected
and there were maggots
crawling out of her smile

I once tried
to jump as high as I could
on a moon-bounce
I thought I could flip
I thought I could fly
I was wrong
and kneed myself in the face
and bled for a week straight
and busted my lip
Now every time I kiss
I remind myself
to not reach so high

I don’t understand people
who don’t wear costumes
to costume parties
It’s all apart of the fun
pretending to be someone
you’re not.

Last year I wanted to dress up as a Car Alarm
but people said that
it would be annoying.
All I ever wanted to do
was to make people notice
the burglars
carrying away their battery
but leaving the lights on
and the engine idling

Maybe this year
I’ll dress up as pond scum
and look for someone dressed up as a microscope
so they can make me feel big
Have you ever noticed how
flies love to commit suicide
down your throat
during a
particularly good bike ride?
It’s as if they’re little poets
and they can put wings
to your words
to choke you up
with emotion

I decided not to get stitches
and to let the bump swell
I had to drink water through a straw
and I couldn’t speak so well

So I kept quiet
and even though it hurt

I still shouted in my mind

After a week or so
I woke up to my lip
tingling and itching
dry and cracked
and yawned myself awake
splitting skin and scab
disturbing the hatched maggots
that flew away
carrying poetry

item.title: Ghosts
item.content:encoded:
I sneezed and you said bless you
but I thought you said I miss you
So I asked why

We learned each other’s superstitions
touching roofs running each other’s red lights
kissing knuckles and clicking tongues
to lock pinkie promises tight

I wish people didn’t become ghosts
when they die in each other’s eyes
because I’m tired of people
walking straight through me

Getting ignored is worse than hate
because it means that you’re nothing
not worth the time to
take the effort to answer why

Turns out that I’m just a passing breeze
a wanton freeze-frame in the motion picture
of a VHS B-rate horror flick
an easily forgotten superstition
disappearing into the mist

item.title: Gnarled Knotted Wood
item.content:encoded:
Know where your hinges lie
said the carpenter to the apprentice
so you can tell what will make you bend

Working with my hands
I spent 6 days 17 hours and 43 minutes
making a frame of reference
And then on the seventh day
I burned it down

Jesus was a carpenter
Noah and Moses too
Abraham, Isaac, Jacob.
Most biblical men worked
with gnarled and knotted wood
burnt bushes and staves and stone
dead trees ringed with age
young saplings bent and buckled
to plowshares and pruning hooks

Impatience is a virtue and
you’re old enough to know when I stop counting seconds
it was the seventh seventh time you asked me
if I was alright
that I answered: “I feel uprooted”

In winter you can feel it the most
raised like flames against the sky
lashing out at heaven
limbs askew dancing in the dark
naked and bare

I have seen death at both ends
I have made coffee tables and bookshelves
from the rotted bark of almost embers
beating with hibernation

I have never built an ark

I’ve made myself deaf and blind
so that I can taste the truth as bitter as it is
that the faces of trees
turn inward in these cold months
and the hands of carpenters
become wood

item.title: Harvest Moon
item.content:encoded:
It’s that time again
When a backhanded goodbye is not enough
and you’re looking for a full-frontal face fuck
because the pregnant moon won’t stop bitching and moaning
how it has needs
and all you need is a good fight

so you go out looking
tomcat brawls in back alley dens
where the concrete is as hard as you
and with the metallic taste of blood from biting your own tongue

You feel like you can build a statue out of your own iron

Kick a can
Kill a man
Punch a wall

Bruises are topographical maps showing how high you have climbed
(and how low you can go)

so plant a blood orange
let it choke your garden out like auto-erotic asphyxiation
water it with blood and tears
let it grow like a man
Cut it down in fall
Reap what you have sown
grasp it from its roots and pull until the sky screams
Sickle-celled tang between your fists
squeeze until the juice runs dry
dribbles down your chin

get ready to starve this winter

item.title: Hindsight
item.content:encoded:
Never understood how she could lie to herself so well
I try to sift through discoveries of my ominous omissions like
I’m drowning in quicksand
Advice: “Don’t worry, be happy”
a McFerrin throwback as I throw up
swirling down the toilet bowl is Truth
(we’re all running from something)
It flees the scene like its running from something
as a disapproving witness the fan clicks
Overhead
wagging its finger at me like an old hag
bitterness of self-loathing so sweet on my tongue
while hooligans, vagabonds
villainous vile vermin gnaw my skull
they chip away at the stone-cold countenance
chiseling
graphic profanity
into the recesses of my mind
driving home
Pounding Sledgehammers
Behind my eyes (she had green eyes)
I keep falling into the same pattern
the same cycle
year after year in dancing in life’s highway
SLAM! on the ground
SLAM! hit the floor
SLAM! almost drowned
SLAM! Always Want More
killing myself slowly softly silently
I guess its good practice for later
White lies kill Black ideas
Racism for the colorblind
and my vision has never been 20/20

He likes to invent things
He could build a machine to stitch my soul back together
if He wanted to, he could fix me
we could be happy
at the end of the world
you could find me in Death Valley outrunning the sun
(we’re all running from something)
begging, please carry me away from my burns
I got them cooking breakfast the next morning
I’m in over my head
My mother fell in love with a Liar
I saw how their lives twisted, bent and broke
and I swore not to let my life crash like a wave
my body torn apart by seagulls on the beach
we are all just made of Water
and Water erodes
let yourself flow into me
but you are dammed
up to Barcroft
I’ve stopped caring if I drown
in your eyes (he had brown eyes)
I wonder if God sees the designs I scratched into your back
the drawn out roadmap of us
when I know one night is not enough to take me around the world
the graves they dig for couples
are dug one-by-one
each is buried alone in the ground
because the dead do not fear loneliness
quietly they let worms wiggle through their hearts
when you rested your glasses on my solitary nightstand
did you see how they fractured the light of the lamp
so that the broken colors of the rainbow spilled out like blood
and I was trapped in your prism

item.title: Ice & Flame
item.content:encoded:
I think everyone is a little scarred

you can’t help but understand pain
it has brought you to where you are
scorch marks like a map
curling up legs and down faces
like serpents

pain has brought me to where I am

my ears become feet
and I travel the train-track-stitches
scratches and pock-marked mountains
with my fingernails scrabbling for purchase in your earth
to avoid the heat

There are two kinds of people in this world

you and me we’re fire and ice
Prometheus and Persephone
charcoal and pomegranates
blood and stone
banished in each other

Chained to past mistakes, they forever take

majestic eagles tear at my insides
while you hide in your own Hades
all we ever wanted was spring warmth and comfort
now we know not to reach so high
moonshots die in the cold of space
and flame as they fall
We’re binary stars wrapped in self-made gravity of situations

Either freeze or burn
you have a choice
move like a glacier slowly carving
or flash fire quick all-consuming
both leaving scars on the land in their wake

Eventually all embers grow cold
Eventually all icebergs melt

Come end with me

item.title: ill literate
item.content:encoded:
reading Ginsberg in a bookstore
because that’s what deep introspective people do dammit
It’s literary porn with slick fellatio dreams
more of the same shit I can see online
with less of a figurative flair
The minute you’ve seen Betty white fucking a horse
you’ve been desensitized to most of everything
the sun kissing my face doesn’t awaken me
and the weather is getting colder so I might as well stay in bed
Instead of fucking with my head
it’s a gonzo type of journalistic intrigue with
slavish mind bitches getting drained like batteries
powering the summer heat through winter
Giving everyone acid dreams
If this is the matrix, does it matter if it’s real or not?
if everything is swathed in latex and chrome
it still doesn’t feel like home
We’re just a bunch of cocaine cowboys
riding into the sunset on an electric cool whip zebra

item.title: Insects
item.content:encoded:
Spiders on the bridge
weaving webs by the river
as the train tracks click-clack
spiders drain old bodies dry
leaving carcasses out in the sun
to mummify

Heat makes me hazy
and my grip slips
knocking my bottle loose
beneath the rocker
the slick syrupy sweet
trickles around my bare feet
through the cracks in the sidewalk
I watch the ants get stuck
marching one by one
drowning in the midday sun
caramelizing

I have your art supplies still
beneath my windowsill
where crickets come to people-watch
they sing of brighter tomorrows
when lazy sunbeams
catch cobwebs
and ignite
I paint people-watching pictures
on the palms of my hands
like sunscreen

I am a mayfly
only 24 hours until I die
no time for wasting
trap me in a mason jar
and I’ll fight the crystal
beating against glass
until one of us cracks
spiderwebbing fragments
to catch on
until all wound up
we give
and roast in the sun

item.title: Juglone
item.content:encoded:
Listen to the drone of the keyboards and the scratch of pens
There isn’t much diversity in ecology
It’s the North Face effect
the brand makes the person
so get your iPhone out to Snapchat pictures
instead of paying attention when the teacher talks about extinction

We learned about competition and we
learned about parasitism
There seem to be a lot of things in common
with how we copy from each other’s tests
to move up the bell curve
to survive

As you grow bigger, your population density gets smaller
you get lonelier
The popularity of leaders is measured
in the number of people who want to kill them

my favorite term for plants is self-pruning
They cut off what is not needed
Juglone drips from the walnut to kill those who lie below
while the floor of the forest decays
hear the rustle of dead-tree paper in the classroom

try to survive

item.title: Little Gone Girl
item.content:encoded:
She was that little gone girl
lost in the last throes of summer
sitting on the second story of an abandoned building
she laughed and jumped
Hit the river hard
waters green, she
sunk down into the muck
came up gasping and naked
trying to hide innocence

We made an oath
that little gone girl and I
traded tattoos, scars and slit wrists
and let our blood mix with ink
to the promise of pretending

We called each other names
she called me old habits
and always fell back into me
I called her sunshine
and basked in her warmth as long as I could
until I got burnt

She was a cherry red iron
branding me with her fingertips
I was a cool drink of water
each word frozen like ice in my throat
breathless, speechless, soundless
we made love in a vacuum
it was cold and airless
so she breathed life into me
and we wrapped our bronze bodies into a furnace
melted into each other
golden children eating the sun
drinking the dust
becoming stars

item.title: Matador
item.content:encoded:
He calls bullshit on himself
sinks a little deeper into his chair
between phone calls home
It’s hard to remember to care
swallow silhouettes in a sketchbook
outlines of dreams
depression is an addiction
and it’s hard to keep clean

Run the bulls on the streets of Pamplona
run them tired, ragged, and hot
run the bulls on the streets of the city
run them until they drop

The pen is a needle
carve twisting veins deep
purple blisters on callused hands
the bruises seem the creep
shut eyes to the world
the world shuts it’s eyes to you
with everyone blind
it’s easy to see truth

head-to-tail, hoof-to-horn
The bulls are roped and led by their balls
eyes-fear-wide, nostrils-flare-rage
The bulls are roped and led into stalls

burrito your sorrow
and mix it with bull’s blood
elixirs taste like sleep
so find other drugs
wave your blankets like favors
to the ghost crowd
a matador’s cape
is but a funeral shroud

oily-mustard trumpets
scream the siren cry
and the mustachioed matador
walks to where he’ll die

Straight ramrod at the center
make yourself taller than you are
when the bulls overtake you
show them where to scar
the crowd shouts for blood
the bulls echoes madness
in Madrid there’s a stake burning for the loser of the contest

he’s magic with the cape
red-fire from his hands
a stumbling-serenade stampede
split-hooves kick up sand

the crowd swells like rippling muscles
teeth gnaw your tongue to rawhide
time waits breathless
for the few remaining strides
hands tremble tension
sword flash, the reflection of eyes
the bull always becomes the matador
so either way you’ll die

Blade drives deep into the heart
Horns into a human sheath
matador and bull as one
relax in eternal sleep

item.title: Melon Moonshine
item.content:encoded:
I’m bushwhacked
weeds choking my heels
and I stumble on the beaten path
dragging along the spoils of war
3 feet of tempered steel
that my Grandpa got off a dead Japanese colonel in Guadalcanal
drawing a line in the dirt with the point and howling at the moon

In my inheritance
there were plenty of hearts to go around
from when he took three shots
and kept fighting
eventually he spent them up to
quadruple bypass mistakes
and drink to make better forgotten memories

I tried to one-up him
I stopped after getting shots five times
because I was feeling light-headed from blood-loss or drinks tossed
I don’t know

but I do know
that I was at that perfect point and time
when stupidity and youth
makes impossible happen

So we found a 19-year-old TV
and beat it to shit
breaking pool cues and hammers
until it threw up glass and electric insides
in our yearly reenactment
of that scene from Office Space
we let ourselves be senseless and violent for brief moments
to make sanity taste sweet like slices of summer watermelon

I took the katana
and clutched it like
a lifeline to shores of former youth
island hopping
crouch low
don’t want to get hit
t-ball stance
fruit ninja this bitch
wait for the pitch
coming right at me
swing slice split straight in half
rotten fruit falls to the side
so I eat the rind

item.title: Memento
item.content:encoded:
The sands were black
and the dying light caught
struggling in the center of the hourglass
pushing up mountains
Lives lay naked on the shore
Wind whipped bear backs
and I walked

Excuse me miss
but you seemed to have
dropped your eyes
They were heavy-lidded and
fluttered out of your grasp
Are you a dream?
Are you a tourist?
Do you need help?

I am a sight seer
I am a nautilus
I am a golden gate
I am a bridge to your chorus.
I feel like a tourist when I come home
I do not need your help

She wouldn’t take her eyes back
She continued as a leper
dropping pieces of herself
as love letters to faded footsteps
Blind into the ocean
Dissolving
How can you miss someone you’ve never met?
How come there are some you never forget?

I pocketed her eyes as memento

I reached deep in my throat, ripped out my voice
and skipped it ventriloquized against the waves
I swapped skin for sun and lungs for air and hands for water and earth for body
Each nerve shrieking seagull
each finger falling tidepool
I pulled my mind apart and
stopped dreaming

I tore myself apart and followed her

item.title: Mona Lisa
item.content:encoded:
So I’ve had this bad case of regret-fueled nostalgia
It’s like insomnia but with a badder bite and it keeps me up at nights
After I get sick with alcohol and turn to you
Your number is blazed into my phone in telephonic code
and the later it gets the less I text until
Hey girl what are you up to? You free? DTF?
Until it’s finally just a solitary question mark
with its back bent with the weight of secrets
spine twisted with scoliosis of the soul
head raised to the sky in a barbaric yawp at the full moon
We’re both loony and I can’t control myself

they say that Misery loves company and Loneliness is her best friend
they were down for a threesome but I ended up with Cowardice at the end
And what’s funny is no matter how much I try to pretend
I still knew she had a boyfriend

I belong in an asylum
because every touch get is electric shock therapy that reinforces
the deadening of emotion
I’m trapped in the padded-walled cell of my mind’s commotion
and the only solution is this vicious cycle of meaningless sex
If it was meaningless why do I always want to make her breakfast the day after
If it was meaningless why do we always dissolve into laughter
It’s that laugh attack that feels like a heart attack
and although I’m an EMT I was never trained for this
I die each time and she always brings be back with mouth-to-mouth
Doesn’t matter that my first sexual encounter
was with a girl that wouldn’t even kiss me
doesn’t matter that after she was done she didn’t even miss me
because brailed lies imprinted on thighs, sighs, oh my, tongue tips touch lips
My carefully constructed marionette of a body pulled along by her fingertips
all it takes is her soft breath to bring me crumbling down. What now?

pretend.

pretend like she don’t matter
like you’re ticking off the days ‘til the end of the month
like every time I see her she doesn’t disassemble my insides
And wrench my guts up and tie me like they’re fuzzy cuffs
I don’t even know if I’m into that stuff
I wonder if she can see through my act
This laser-eyed beauty drawing and quartering me
Uncurling what we’ve agreed can’t happen
Demanding a confession of how lost I am
In the desert wasteland
Of your Mona Lisa smile

item.title: Peanut Butter and Bananas
item.content:encoded:
I broke down crying
making peanut butter banana slices
and grilled cheese
cut in triangles
because no matter how well I made it
it would never taste the same
as the nights I would pad downstairs
from a nightmare
for a midnight snack
and my mom would pour me a glass of milk
and talk troubles away

Now
sitting on the floor of my kitchen
nose running
I wonder if she ever thought her peanut butter banana slices weren’t good enough
they weren’t close enough to how her mom made them
they only tasted like regret
with a dollop of nostalgia
and she ended up on the floor of her kitchen
after I padded back upstairs

item.title: Poetry
item.content:encoded:
I once made a promise to Poetry that I couldn’t keep
I told her that I’d write her name on my sleeve
but I burned that shirt to keep warm
in an oil-drum fire with some old mementos
that I had kept in a box since 1st grade
I roasted the pictures medium-rare eating memories to keep me alive
until I’m half empty-full

Well take a minute to look at this picture
It’s 3am and we’re sitting in my car
before we decided not to take off our clothes
and you ask me why I never write poems about you as if it is easy
as if these words are not painstakingly ripped from my heart
I give you a half-ass non-committal verbal shrug
that sounds like most of my conversations
with other people

the real reason
is because you are a mirror
I wouldn’t want to stare too long
or risk going blind
staring down infinity
if home is a drain
it makes sense that we keep circling
vultures feeding on each other
picking ourselves apart

You are a crossroads
lost and sold
You are the apple
stare green and gold
You are a mockingbird
cry freedom to the morning
You are a moon dance
pour your liquid body out whole

I am a ghost
a shadow on a silver-lining
I am a riptide
drown beneath my waves
I am a memory
a fallen tree in a forest
I am a poet
I make promises I can’t keep

item.title: Rollercoaster
item.content:encoded:
You know how roller coasters pause on the cusp?
They make you think that they’ve crashed or rust-ed
and that you’ll always stay on the brink
Never thinking that it’ll all come crashing down all at once
only to swoop back up again

but for that one moment
you’re terrified
before the ride of your life

Everything slows down
and speeds up
everyone puts their hands up
scream and yell
forget that you have secrets you have yet to tell
and I don’t want to give up
but I think I’m getting motion sickness

I saw a bald eagle with clipped wings
and met a girl with a tan-line ring
which just shows me that it’s not about the things you try
but what you don’t

so I’ll split the night
I’ll weather the fight
I’ll speak in black and white
and dream in color

item.title: Salute to an American Home
item.content:encoded:
She was a sock without a pair
making a breakfast of leftovers
using burnt hands
to sculpt two lovers
like clay into hardtack
serving it raw
calling it
morning after medicine

I broke my teeth on her pieces
and choked on tattered remains
of an American flag
throwing it all up

freedom tastes like an empty home

item.title: Sarasota
item.content:encoded:
She said all old jazz musicians end up in Sarasota
before their notes fade in the air
because there’s something about that town
that pickles memories and floats them like fireflies
Waiting to be caught and set alight

In the steamy swamps south of New Orleans
you can hear the yell of a cornet call clear across the bayou
warning that the levee will break
to get back home before dark sinks you back under the mud
The sax screams back
calling down curses in
a hot red angry buzz
and if you listen close, the trombone frogs respond
hopping mad with heat
croaking about how they used to be princes
While the thrum of the bass soothes like dragonfly wings
flapping in time to the snap clap of the crickets
jumping to the snare drum beat
All these magic voodoo animals end up in Sarasota

the lazy smoke of Harlem
plays clarinet like a cigarette drag
syncopating city lights beneath
the neon-clad
it’s always twilight on the fire escapes
and the notes are always so blue
because it’s lonely in the city
Sarasota is calling to you

Chicago is a bragging city
With kick drum boom
and swaggering brass croon
like double-breasted suits
Double bass walks all over town
until it’s wood worn and tired
strings slapping against each other
like half-step siblings
the chromatic chrome street lamps
silhouetted like piano keys at midnight
taking the A-Train
to Sarasota

There’s only one street in the hot tin town
it’s one-way with a dead end
it twists and turns like a harmonica bend
and there’s a parade through every night
with Louie and Charlie and Duke and Ella
leading to the graveyard
It’s always a party there
Skeletons beat bones on
headstones like vibraphone keys
funeral jazz is slow and sweet
play til you’re on your knees
all old jazz musicians always end up
in Sarasota

item.title: Shitty Love Poetry #1
item.content:encoded:
Can I find religion in you?
In your hair, in your stare, in the little way you bite your lip
and how you always eat things by sticking out your tongue tip…
If I write you shitty love poetry is that a cliché? Am I “gay?”
If so then call me Liberachi, let me worship Neil Patrick Harris’s body
let’s get fucked up on Bicardi and move to Vermont so I can be gay for you
In my mind that wouldn’t be a bad thing to do because my religion is you

I might not go to church
but I believe in a different kind of god than the biblical sort
You can find my god in the steam your breath makes
on the first true day of autumn
or in the idea of a sunny patch
or in the amazing way babies babble
and you understand exactly what they’re saying because
they’re trying to explain what living feels like

You’re so much like poison ivy; keeping me itching
if you were a chef I would be your kitchen
and all we would make would be cheese dishes
because even though you’re a lac-tard
I just want to show you how grate-ful I am
and we can be cheesy together
I’m such a dope around you because I’m addicted and you’re my heroine
Never a villainess but whenever I see you in a dress its villainy
because I have a vendetta against when you wear clothes.
All those soft moans. All these nights I spend alone.
I go through paper after paper as fast as I can so you can tell
how much I pine for you
I could cover you in maple syrup and still only be 39% done
with kissing your body
It’d be sticky but you’d be my pancake and whenever my heart would ache
we could have breakfast in bed

Please remember what you just read, let it fill your head
with the promise of nights that blend into tomorrows
of days filled to the brim
If I could swallow you whole just to carry you around inside of me I would
but we haven’t gone to Jonah’s in awhile
and I’m not whale even though I pretend to be sometimes
So take this as a compliment and shake the fever out
so that I can hold you until my fire dies down
and we can freeze hell over together
It’s okay. We can share my sweater.

item.title: Siren Call
item.content:encoded:
Richmond before rain
drives me insane
The city summer sky bends and breaks
and heaven cries for relief
streets deserted
except for the train
that you can hear whistle and moan
like a mourning mother
clear across town
while we chain smoke like guns.

from above
You can see black dots
rushing to hide last minute
as if you could hide yourself from this
wave
slicks the street with bodies
dancing and drowning
becoming a tide of broken homes
the city gasping
while acid eats bones black
our sidewalk covered with
mementos to dissolving dark bodies
Wizard of Oz style
so that when the light hits the water just right
It mixes like blood

I heard gunshots outside my window last night
Staccato cracks in the black
man I wanted to be a man when I moved here but
I’m scared I’ll never reach
Twenty-one homicides in the past
nine months, the city pregnant with rage
mother Richmond raising bullet babies
that eat each other in the womb
When I first moved here
I thought the city was infested with woodpeckers
trying to eat their way out of wood
only to make their own coffins
but I realized I was dead wrong
now I know when I hear death flap its wings
it’s a murder of black birds
with sirens screaming “nevermore”

Jackson Ward is a prison yard
blackmaled into dreaming
you can escape
but there’s a war going on
with 5-to-6-foot something, wearing something, toting something
soldiers trying to take Oregon Hill
18 to 20 something serving 18 to 20 something
while the city Shockoe Slips back into the
Tobacco Row where we were raised
as plantation slaves
and it won’t be long before it all becomes another Hollywood Cemetery with a headstone that reads:
“I once had a dream”

I love playing the game gunshot or firework
on my back porch
it gets harder because we
drink ourselves blind and mute
while celebrating freedom
ignoring the gasps from the gutter
we could see him being
beaten black
and blue
black
and blue
lights paint empty faces
from a parking lot away
because we were too afraid
to say anything
to help a fellow human being
he was beaten by chains he could not break.
uncomfortable
we went inside
but could still hear his animal cries

Those same tears
work like lubricant
for a back-alley score
talking about love like love’s a whore
“she looks like she can take a dick”
“damn look at that ass”
“let me fuck that, baby”

you know nothing about forgiveness
I was beaten
until my lip cracked
and my head bled
red sea split
coughed on my own blood
refused IV drip
metallic and bitter iron

can’t you see my father’s father was once a slave?
chest marked by a bone yellow star

dreads coming down his back
strangling his skull
fist flying
feet flapping
running always running
Exodus

she cried vengeance
over my broken body
but I bled out my anger
forgiveness flows easy
from the side of plenty
all I wanted to know
was why

River city red rain funeral train
Jett Higham, 18 they blew out his brains
a few blocks away
innocent
all he wanted was something sweet from life
so who is to blame?

who is to blame?

item.title: Snow / Sun
item.content:encoded:
soft static drifts
chill me to the bone
as your joy turns to ashes in your mouth
write me a religion
bury me in an old folks home
race a mountain
break the ice
dive deep and come up shivering

I’ll dig a fire
in the pits of your eyes
as the avalanche of your hair
smothers me
spit freezes on our lips
while I dig down
to find warmth
at the core
frostbitten and sore
I let your storm take me

Remember that time we went racing?
You and I, the sand kicking our backs
the wind biting our heels
we ran
You looked at me
and I looked at you
and I swear I saw us go supernova
in your gold eyes
we melted
and fell like droplets
on the face of the earth
crashing into the surf

When did we go?
when did we let time unravel
the womb-baskets of our bodies
like armor
we crumble
we break
let my limbs rust with you
until we can no longer start until each step
leaves pieces of us behind
footsteps in the sand

item.title: Uncertain
item.content:encoded:
It was when we were driving back from Florida
mostly lost
that I asked you why there wasn’t a better way to describe uncertainty
Not in the sense of standing on the brink looking into the void
being at the precipice of unknown
but more in the murky sense of searching
you were quiet for a bit then said:
“It’s like searching for objects in a glass of milk”
or maybe it’s like swimming in milk
grasping at any kind of cheerios life raft you can find
even if some are broken
or some don’t fit on your spoon
“It’s like starting a story in the middle” I answered
where the ending isn’t written
and you don’t know the beginning well enough
to figure out where you are

being uncertain is like prison inmates exercising before death row sentencing
or pretending to be the person you have to be

I am in the void, off of the edge, already squinting in the black
searching for signal in noise

We kept driving
passing millions of strangers
still uncertain of where we were

item.title: Untitled #Drunk
item.content:encoded:
Huffing fumes
I put on my downstairs shoes
and try not to let my floor suck me down

Holding molten potions of booze
Drunk and confused
Dressed to the best as an American clown

I try to choose
but my brain has fused
So I walk down the block in this strange town

Breathing the blues
I become my own muse
and pretend the end is in the air so I drown

item.title: We Go
item.content:encoded:
We skip
class we buy
bus tickets to Richmond we break
into the Interbake we smoke
stacks into the sides of factories we write
promises on walls we white-wash
our war faces we go
we go
we go
we breathe fog
on the river we bless
lady liberty with song we dangle
toes off docks we sweat
with the rhythm of Fridays
You are what you
are what you
eat what you leave
behind we trash
bottles and we break
bones and we love
life as art we are
art we make
love

item.title: When you love a woman
item.content:encoded:
understand that you love an echo
understand that you love an iceberg
understand that you love a clock
together you’ll melt, lose time and yell until
your heart will give out
and her shadow will be a blanket
and her breath a religion
and her torso a stanza
to whisper feverishly in the dark

item.title: Widdershins
item.content:encoded:
You know that magic trick?
Where there’s two rings
or more
and the magician strings them together
into chains
with a wave of his wand?

Abracadabra

I see magic everywhere
friends become disappearing acts
now you see them
now you don’t
notice the black rings under their eyes
that’s the key to this trick

The most magical time of night
is 4 am leaning over a bridge
levitating above the road
caught in the circle of light
of a streetlamp
like a moth
waiting for it to flicker out
I like watching the circles of headlights pass by
wishing I was brave enough
to swallow a flame

I have friends who are fire-eaters
but most just like blowing smoke rings
and laugh because I can’t
even though I always try
A burning circle of coal
lit our faces that night
as we talked about how we always come back
to the same people
over and over
because there’s no tricks to them
and that’s the real magic

When we had enough
of poking holes into our souls
and clouding our minds with smoke
so that our thoughts choked up
and our words flowed freely
I walked her home
and tried to blow smoke rings
into the cold air
I kissed her goodnight
and tasted ashes
on her tongue ring
as my breath and hers
twisted into infinity

Let me let you in on a secret:
the key to the trick is a small gap
held hidden in the magician’s hand
if you aren’t distracted
you can see how he flits back and forth
between bound and free

Magic.

item.title: winter is a cold memory
item.content:encoded:
The moon was a toenail
the day we left
and I wanted to give myself hiccups on that cold January night
watching as
she kissed him deep
in the parking lot of the metro
and then waltzed back home
shins skyscraped
from a city boy’s stubble

I reminisced about what we never made
hands in my pockets
thinking that
my friends are like a box
full of mismatched gloves
sputtering
gently we run
batteries on empty
writing in each others yearbooks
then passing it on

My breath mingled with your smokestacks
as we drove
while the air between us was empty
between each rattling toke

They have me taking sun supplements now
because when you bury yourself
starving
nostalgia is a needle infusion
of pre-chewed sunlight

and so we sat in silence
everything had already been said

She asked why I was quiet
and I answered:
“because it is loud in my head”
